Question 1What are we trying to achieve? See the diagram →

GoalAI is designed, governed and used so that it strengthens cooperation and flourishing at the individual, organisational, societal and planetary scales, rather than extracting from them.From Paul Atkins and David Sloan Wilson (document)
← All statementsWhat are we trying to achieve?
Goal

AI is designed, governed and used so that it strengthens cooperation and flourishing at the individual, organisational, societal and planetary scales, rather than extracting from them.

Shown in diagrams as: “AI strengthens cooperation and flourishing at every scale.”

Where it sits

Contributed by
AI assistant
Ideas from
Paul Atkins and David Sloan Wilson
Standing
Proposed; no one has accepted it yet

Where this comes from

  • Paul Atkins and David Sloan Wilson, Evolving Prosocial AI · How We Shape the Systems that Shape AI - and Us · p. 9, Defining Prosocial AI

    Paraphrased by the AI from this supplied document.

  • Paul Atkins and David Sloan Wilson, Evolving Prosocial AI · How We Shape the Systems that Shape AI - and Us · pp. 35–36, Alignment Across Scales

    Reconstructed by the AI from the supplied passage.

A credit says where an idea comes from, not that its author agrees with this wording. None of the people credited has reviewed it.

Connections

  • Leads into · is needed forPeople's competence, autonomy and relatedness grow through their use of AI rather than wearing away.
  • Leads into · is needed forOrganisations that build AI treat it as a commons: those who contribute data, labour and creative work share in its benefits and have a real say in how it is run.
  • Leads into · is needed forAI strengthens democratic participation, shared facts and the capacity of institutions, and widens real opportunity for marginalised groups.
  • Leads into · is needed forAI's full lifecycle costs in energy, water and materials are accounted for, and it is designed to work within planetary boundaries and with ecological knowledge.
  • Leads into · is needed forInstitutional arrangements make cooperation more rewarding than extraction, so prosocial AI does not depend on self-sacrifice against competitive pressure.
  • Leads into · is needed forThose who design, govern and use AI hold worldviews that value capability, interdependence and effects across scales, and treat AI's direction as a collective choice rather than an inevitability.
